semantics.quests: per quest already present in rules.json: `add` appends a rule of a kind the quest does not have; `replace` overwrites the params of an existing kind; `remove` drops a kind
semantics.new_quests: quests absent from rules.json: full rule list (tier from out/questdata/risk.json, questline fixed)
semantics.proposed_kinds: justified proposals for kinds outside the 16 in tools/coverage/rules.py; NOT usable until L9/L4 accept them; every rule that needs one also carries an existing-kind fallback in quests/new_quests

funcs_vocabulary_extension.doc: PartyAwareCond.funcs keys known to tools/coverage/rules.py: GetDistance GetInCell GetInSameCell IsActionRef IsKiller GetAV(GetActorValue) GetEquipped GetInWorldspace. Dead Money reads these further player-bound functions (counts in gaps.md); the patch proposes the reduction for each.

NVDLC01MQ00.why: Bunker gas trap is the real entry. OnTrigger <player> only fires for the host player; the party must be in the bunker interior and be warped together (hazards ENTRY-TRIGGER/CONTROLS/STRIP/TIMER/MQ00).

params.note: RemoveAllItems -> own stash per slot; see proposed kind PerPlayerState(stash)

NVDLC01MQ01.why: Stage 5 equips the collar, jumpsuit and holorifle on `player`; XP for the whole DLC is scaled once from Player.GetLevel.

params.note: EquipItem of jumpsuit/collar/holorifle must run for every slot (EquipItem is not captured)

NVDLC01MQ01a.why: Dog recruit: the command note stage trigger reads the host's notes; hire grants a player perk.

NVDLC01MQ01b.why: Dean recruit: pickpocket/sneak check and hire perk.

NVDLC01MQ01c.why: Christine recruit: scripted power-off in the basement and her Signal Interference perk.

NVDLC01MQ01d.why: Act transition at the fountain: story-critical, the party has to be together before Elijah's briefing.

NVDLC01MQ02a.why: Dog Gala: quest script counts GhostHarvesterRemains for the host player only; terminal autosaves.

NVDLC01MQ02b.why: Dean Gala: companion gear transfer (RemoveAllTypedItems) goes to `player` only; hologram switches are IsActionRef Player.

NVDLC01MQ02c.why: Christine Gala: the elevator ride moves the activator only (Gala02ElevatorDoor MoveTo); the elevator lie costs shared karma once.

NVDLC01MQ02.why: The existing tether pulls the whole party into the Gala02 switching station, which is only Christine's task. The three Gala tasks happen in three different worldspaces and can run in parallel (a co-op strength). The only shared moment is the bell-tower trigger (stage 50). Tether there; barrier on 'all three roles done'.

NVDLC01MQ03a.why: Kitchen: stealth and talk-down scene ending in `player.kill player 0` / `startcombat player` for the host. Everyone must be inside; Dog's combat target is the initiator.

NVDLC01MQ03b.why: Theatre: hologram security reads Player.IsSneaking / GetHasNote of the host; Dean's key goes to `Player`.

NVDLC01MQ03c.why: Suites: Christine's death starts a 16-30 s collar countdown that kills `player`; the whole party has to leave NVDLC01Suites.

NVDLC01MQ03.why: Vault ending. cells=[] in rules.json makes the tether a no-op; the vault interior EditorID is not in the extracted data (unknown), so tether the Suites that lead to it. The elevator completes the quest for everybody when ONE player uses it: barrier first, then warp all. Failure branches (Elijah team-up, trapped, reading the personal log) end the DLC through MoveTo + StopQuest + a player kill.

NVDLC01MQ03d.why: Dead stub quest (stages empty, only StopQuest at 100); keep out of gating.

NVDLC01DogBarkTimer.why: Bark timer driven by Dog's script (GetPlayerTeammate, IsActionRef Player); barks play for the owner and nearby party.

NVDLC01DeanBarkTimer.why: Bark timer: player.GetSitting in the quest script, Dean's sneak/activate checks.

NVDLC01ChristineBarkTimer.why: Bark timer driven by Christine's script (pickpocket check, teammate flag).

NVDLC01ChristineTerminalFX.why: Terminal effects scene in the Clinic (Christine script, suites elevator IsActionRef Player).

NVDLC01RadioDog.why: Collar radio chatter: plays when Dog is within 2000 units or in the same cell as `player`.

NVDLC01RadioDeanQuest.why: Collar radio chatter for Dean; same distance test as RadioDog.

NVDLC01RadioChristine.why: Collar radio chatter for Christine; same distance test as RadioDog.

NVDLC01Intro.why: Intro slideshow: ~17 narrator INFOs (SayTo Player chain) then StartQuest VillaTransitionTimer.

NVDLC01VillaTransitionTimer.why: Fade, then `player.MoveTo DLC01StartMarker`: moves the host only.

NVDLC01FountainStartSequence.why: Wake-up cinematic at the fountain; at the end it activates Elijah on `Player` (forced conversation) and starts MQ01 stage 5.

NVDLC01Ending.why: Ending slideshow (14 INFOs, SwapTexture per slide) and the failure endings; risk.json scores it T0 because the effects hide in INFO scripts and object scripts (NarratorScript, SlideshowTrigger, SMGateMojave).

NVDLC01BunkerTransitionTimer.why: Ending fade then `player.MoveTo NVDLC01EndMarker` back to the Mojave bunker; returns control.

NVDLC01FadeToCreditsTimer.why: Failure ending: fades out, then `Player.KillActor` on the host to force an autosave reload. Must become a session-level end for all players.

NVDLC01BombCollarQuest.why: The collar state machine: iNumRadii, fCollarTimer, bBoom, rDeadFollower ... are single quest variables; timeout kills `player`.

params.note: fallback until PerPlayerState exists: one collar record per slot

NVDLC01RadioSpeakers.why: Collar emitters (speakers/radios) measure GetDistance player; their radius test must run per slot.

NVDLC01GlobalToxicDamage.why: Villa-wide cloud damage on PlayerREF (Hardcore only).

NVDLC01ToxicCloud.why: Local toxic cloud volumes; damage to PlayerREF.

NVDLC01Followers.why: Companion command topics (323 INFOs): hire/fire/wait/tactics and the single rCurrentFollower slot.

NVDLC01NewVegasFollowerFireQuest.why: On entry, SetPlayerTeammate 0 on every New Vegas companion (Boone, Arcade, Cass, Lily, Veronica, Raul, Rex, ED-E): must dismiss each player's companions and park them in the Mojave.

NVDLC01DogDialogue.why: 454 INFOs, 130 scripted; Dog/God personality switch, kitchen scene, gala.

NVDLC01DeanDialogue.why: 389 INFOs, 96 scripted; theatre fight, karma changes (+/-25).

NVDLC01ChristineDialogue.why: 326 INFOs, 60 scripted; the elevator lie, the suites fight, karma +25.

NVDLC01ElijahDialogue.why: 216 INFOs, 54 scripted; the vault intercom decides the ending (team-up = failure).

NVDLC01CasinoComps.why: Chip exchange with the hologram cashier: pre-war money and chips are per-player currency, NOT quest items.

NVDLC01ChipReward.why: After the DLC: 100 Sierra Madre Chips every 3 game days into one drop box (container); a shared container is first-come.

params.note: AddItem on a container is not captured (itemOnNonPlayer); needs a per-slot drop box or AddItem to each player

NVDLC01GalaEventQuest.why: Dialogue that fires the Gala (SetStage NVDLC01MQ02 50).

params.vars: script variables to shard per slot

proposed_kinds.justification: PerPlayerScene routes the effects of ONE scene to the originating player. Dead Money has four continuous per-player state machines that live in single script variables and run for the whole DLC: the bomb collar (NVDLC01BombCollarQuestSCRIPT: iNumRadii, fCollarTimer, bBoom, rDeadFollower, fDeathTimer, ...; also the vault, suite and kitchen timers), the Villa toxic cloud (iToxicCloudsActive, per-frame DamageActorValue on PlayerREF), the equipment stash (one container NVDLC01PlayerEquipmentContainerRef for all players) and the companion slot (NVDLC01Followers.rCurrentFollower/bHaveCompanion). With N players each needs N independent instances, host-driven timers per slot, and Recipient=slot on every kill/damage/message. Without it every fix is a one-off in the hooks. Data model in policy_review.md section 'PerPlayerState'.
